Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful demo and discussion. A couple of procurement/legal folks asked for a short written confirmation on what Redwood stores when we send prompts/receive outputs to the hosted API. Specifically:

- Are prompts or model outputs persisted (logs, telemetry, or otherwise)?
- If stored, where are they stored and for how long?
- Are there any options to disable retention or keep data only in our region?
- How are PII elements handled (redaction, masking) in logs/monitoring?

Could you provide a concise summary we can include in an internal procurement packet? If you have a short PDF or SOC2 excerpt that covers this, that would be great.

Hi Katie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (Security & Privacy) and Marissa (Customer Success) to provide the official summary and attachments. Below is a short recap and we'll follow up with a concise one-page statement for procurement.

Summary (high-level):
- By default, Redwood collects request metadata (timestamps, model used, token counts) and stores prompts/outputs transiently for 30 days for abuse prevention, quality monitoring, and platform improvements.
- Customers on enterprise Dedicated or Private deployments can opt into no-retention configurations; Private deployments can be configured to never send prompts/outputs to Redwood-hosted storage.
- Data is stored encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Access is strictly controlled and logged.
- We support region pinning for hosted logs (US / EU) and offer customer-managed key options for Private deployments.

Neha/Marissa — please add details / confirm retention windows and any exceptions.

Best,

Hi Katie — thanks for raising these. Below is a concise confirmation you can share with procurement/legal. I kept it factual and implementation-level so you can paste into a vendor questionnaire or SOW. If you need a redlined clause we can provide one.

Official PII handling confirmation (prompts & outputs):
1) What is stored?
   - Request metadata: timestamps, model identifier/version, token counts, route/endpoint, and anonymized latency/error metrics.
   - Prompts and model outputs: by default, prompts and outputs are retained to support abuse detection, debugging, and to improve model-serving quality.

2) Retention windows and purpose
   - Hosted (default) customers: prompts/outputs retained for 30 days. Logs/metrics retained per plan (30–90 days).
   - Dedicated (reserved capacity): retention is configurable; standard enterprise commits include options for 30 days, 90 days, or custom retention.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): no data is sent to Redwood control-plane storage by default unless explicitly enabled; customers control retention policies.
   - Purpose limitations: retained data is used solely for platform operations (monitoring, debugging, abuse prevention) unless the customer opts in for model improvements.

3) PII handling and redaction
   - Automated redaction: our logging pipeline masks commonly recognized PII patterns (SSNs, credit cards, emails, phone numbers) in operational traces. This is applied to logs and non-persistent debug dumps.
   - Customer-controlled redaction: customers can enable additional redaction rules at the routing layer (e.g., regex-based) prior to being written to any storage.
   - Human access: access to raw prompts/outputs is restricted to a small set of authorized engineers for incident response and only after approval workflows; all access is audited.

4) Data residency & encryption
   - Residency: hosted logs can be pinned to US or EU regions. Private deployments keep data entirely within customer-managed networks/regions.
   - Encryption: data encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated and Private deployments.

5) Options to disable retention / opt-out
   - Opt-out for hosted: available on enterprise plans via contractual terms (data-retention opt-out / dedicated buffer).
   - Dedicated/Private: customers can configure zero-retention modes or route logs to their own storage.

6) Compliance & evidence
   - We are SOC 2 Type II audited; redacted SOC2 report attached.
   - Product privacy summary attached (one-pager).

7) Next steps we recommend for Acme Health
   - If you need zero-retention for PHI/PII: pursue Private (VPC) deployment or Dedicated with zero-retention config.
   - For procurement: we can provide a short vendor statement and a redlined data processing clause.

Attachments: product-privacy-summary.pdf, soc2-report-redacted.pdf

If you'd like, I can produce a one-paragraph vendor statement for the procurement packet and an explicit SOW clause.
